transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-01-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Arielle Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Vale (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Liam Ortiz (Marinera CISO), Rina Park (Marinera Head of Infra), Omar Castillo (Marinera Compliance), Sofia Mendes (Marinera Legal), Noah Green (Marinera SRE)

Summary:
Quick posture review covering Redwood's SOC 2 / ISO 27001 artifacts, trust portal access, RBAC/SSO options, audit log retention and the proposed KMS integration flow. Customer focused on EU data residency, key rotation procedures, and a controls mapping for their internal audit.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 report scope and availability (shared artifacts)
- Trust Portal access (roles/RBAC for auditors)
- SSO/SAML provisioning and SCIM sync cadence
- Audit logs: retention, format, export (parquet/csv) and SIEM integration
- Data residency: region pinning and cross-region fallbacks
- Encryption/KMS: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options, rotation, and HSM-backed keys
- Controls mapping: mapping Redwood controls to Marinera control IDs

Action items (abbreviated): see metadata section for owners/dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Arielle Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll run through the posture artifacts and then hand over to Marcus for the KMS walkthrough, um, and leave time for questions at the end.
[00:00:12] Liam Ortiz: thanks Arielle, quick ask — can we confirm the iso scope, like is it platform only or does it include data plane in eu regions?
[00:00:22] Arielle Chen: good question. the SOC2/ISO bundle we share today covers the control plane and hosted inference, and we have an appendix that lists region coverage — eu regions are in scope for the hosted product as of last audit, um there's a separate note for private deployments. i'll attach the PDF.
[00:00:41] Rina Park: so just to be clear — if we use Redwood hosted in eu, logs and tokens stay in eu? what about backups?
[00:00:52] Marcus Vale: short answer: yes for primary artifacts, backups depend on retention tier, we have a policy that egress for backups can be restricted to the region for enterprise tenants; we can show the configuration in the trust portal.
[00:01:10] Noah Green: i need to know whether we can require key material never leave our KMS — we plan to do BYOK.
[00:01:18] Marcus Vale: BYOK is supported. we do an envelope encryption model — the customer key (in your KMS) wraps a data key used by the runtime. the wrapped key material is stored encrypted, and we support HSM-backed keys in aws ksm and gcp cloud kms — there's also a rotation flow.
[00:01:39] Omar Castillo: rotation flow, is that automatic or manual? auditors will ask about key rotation cadence and evidence.
[00:01:45] Marcus Vale: rotation can be automated via a rotation policy or you can trigger manual rotations. we'll provide logs for key usage and rotation events to the audit trail; those events are sent to the trust portal and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[00:02:01] Sofia Mendes: do you have an example audit artifact for key rotation we can include in our control mapping?
[00:02:06] Arielle Chen: yes, we'll include a sample key-rotation audit report, it's in the trust center artifacts bundle — i'll drop the link after the call (Link: https://trust.redwood.ai/artifacts/SOC2-ISO-bundle-2024).
[00:02:22] Liam Ortiz: walking back to RBAC — can we restrict auditors to read-only access to logs and prevent them from requesting model rollbacks or snapshots?
[00:02:32] Priya Nair: absolutely — we've got role templates. auditor role is read-only for trust artifacts and audit logs, it can't trigger rollbacks; app-level roles control model operations. we also support time-bound access for 3rd-party auditors.
[00:02:48] Rina Park: how does SSO provisioning work? we use Okta and want SCIM to auto-provision groups.
[00:02:55] Marcus Vale: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. group sync frequency is configurable; default is every 15 minutes, you can change to hourly. there are a few attributes we require, we'll share a SCIM mapping doc.
[00:03:10] Noah Green: about audit logs, what's the retention default and is export immediate? we need raw logs for 7 years for one of our regions.
[00:03:18] Marcus Vale: default retention on hosted is 90 days for high-volume logs, but enterprise tenants can configure longer retention — we have an add-on for extended retention up to 7 years via cold storage. export is available via scheduled exports or API on-demand. format is jsonl or parquet.
[00:03:35] Omar Castillo: for the controls mapping, we need a crosswalk between our control IDs and the Redwood controls — do you provide a matrix?
[00:03:41] Arielle Chen: yes, we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps to SOC 2 trust services criteria and iso 27001 Annex A. we'll populate a column for Marinera's control IDs. i'll send a template.
[00:03:55] Liam Ortiz: any gotchas on egress? we need to ensure nothing leaves eu except for aggregated telemetry if we opt in.
[00:04:03] Marcus Vale: there are two egress lanes — telemetry and data egress. telemetry can be configured to be anonymized and you can opt out. for data egress, we honor region pinning and do not replicate data to other regions unless you enable cross-region DR.
[00:04:20] Rina Park: can we get an architecture diagram for the private deployment option? we may need to host on-prem for certain regulated shipments.
[00:04:28] Arielle Chen: yes, Marcus has a private deployment reference diagram. we also have an on-prem appliance blueprint.
[00:04:35] Marcus Vale: i'll share the infra blueprint and a checklist — network ports, firewall rules, required IAM roles, and the KMS handshake flow.
[00:04:43] Sofia Mendes: legal question — is there an SLAs addendum for data residency? we want contractual guarantees.
[00:04:49] Arielle Chen: for enterprise contracts we can include data residency commitments in the MSA with remedies and audit rights, we'll loop in legal after the call.
[00:05:00] Liam Ortiz: back to logging — what fields do you log on inference requests? we need user-id, request-id, model id, region, and masked prompt, not full text.
[00:05:10] Marcus Vale: we log request-id, model version, shard location, latency metrics, and masked prompt hash. full prompts are redactable — we can configure redaction and tokenization to keep only embeddings or hashes.
[00:05:26] Noah Green: can we configure TTL for cached KV so PHI isn't kept longer than necessary?
[00:05:31] Marcus Vale: yes, prefix/KV cache TTLs are configurable per route, and you can set aggressive eviction for regulated data. we recommend not caching PHI.
[00:05:41] Rina Park: is there an audit trail when RBAC changes happen? we need evidence for SOC 2.
[00:05:45] Priya Nair: RBAC changes are versioned and logged with who/when/what. the trust portal exposes that as an audit artifact and you can download csv.
[00:05:56] Omar Castillo: for the controls mapping, can you map Redwood controls to our internal control numbers and include evidence links?
[00:06:02] Arielle Chen: yes we'll create a three-column map: Marinera control, Redwood control, evidence link. evidence link will point to artifacts in the trust portal.
[00:06:12] Liam Ortiz: how fast can you grant auditor access? sometimes audits are scheduled last minute.
[00:06:16] Priya Nair: we can provision auditor access within 24 hours for enterprise accounts; for temporary time-bound SSO we can generate limited tokens that expire.
[00:06:25] Rina Park: we have a secondary ask: can we force MFA for all admin console logins?
[00:06:29] Marcus Vale: yes, MFA is enforced for admin roles and can be required for all users if you prefer.
[00:06:36] Arielle Chen: quick pause — i'm going to drop two links in the chat: the SOC2 bundle and a controls mapping template.
[00:06:42] Arielle Chen: Link: https://trust.redwood.ai/artifacts/SOC2-ISO-bundle-2024
[00:06:47] Arielle Chen: Template: https://trust.redwood.ai/templates/controls-mapping-mariner-template.xlsx
[00:06:52] Liam Ortiz: perfect.
[00:07:00] Noah Green: on KMS integration, we need to test a failover scenario where the customer KMS endpoint is unreachable — what happens to inference requests?
[00:07:07] Marcus Vale: we support a fallback policy: if the KMS is unreachable we can fail closed or fail open depending on your risk appetite. for Marinera i'd recommend fail closed with an alert to your ops channel and a queued retry — that provides safest posture.
[00:07:23] Rina Park: will fail closed cause downtime, and will that violate our SLAs?
[00:07:27] Marcus Vale: it could cause brief request denial. we document it in the SLA with an exception for customer-managed KMS outages. we can also recommend a secondary managed KMS as standby.
[00:07:41] Omar Castillo: can you provide the raw audit log schema? our GRC team wants to ingest to their SIEM.
[00:07:47] Marcus Vale: yes, there is a schema doc and a sample kafka/parquet export. i'll attach it — likewise we have a sample lambda to ingest into common SIEMs.
[00:07:58] Arielle Chen: quick note — competitors were brought up earlier, CloudAI and FastServe; we don't do comparative slides here but i can share a capabilities matrix.
[00:08:08] Liam Ortiz: let's get back to evidence for iso27001 annex a controls mapping to our auditors. is the scope limited to hosted product?
[00:08:15] Arielle Chen: the current ISO attestation covers the hosted inference product and control plane; for Dedicated/Private we have separate SOC references and an architecture addendum.
[00:08:26] Priya Nair: if you decide on Dedicated, we can run a gap analysis for the private deployment and add the missing controls to the mapping.
[00:08:33] Rina Park: any notes on data deletion? we need a certified deletion proof for certain countries.
[00:08:38] Marcus Vale: we provide a data deletion certificate that includes deletion timestamps and hashes for destroyed keys or blobs. for backups we have a wipe-and-verify flow.
[00:08:51] Noah Green: can we get a walk-through of the trust portal UI so we know where to download artifacts and how to grant auditor access?
[00:08:56] Arielle Chen: yes, Priya will run a short demo in the follow-up session — we'll schedule it as a separate 30 minute session.
[00:09:04] Priya Nair: I'll post the demo invite for the week of 01/26.
[00:09:12] Liam Ortiz: last question on evidence: do you store SHA256 of artifacts so we can prove artifact integrity?
[00:09:19] Marcus Vale: yes, artifacts are hashed and signed, and we provide checksums and signature verification procedure in the trust portal.
[00:09:29] Arielle Chen: ok, sounds like we have clear next steps — Marcus will do the KMS diagram and test plan, i'll send the SOC2 bundle and the controls template, and Priya will schedule the trust portal demo. any other final questions?
[00:09:44] Sofia Mendes: from legal side we'll want the MSA redline for residency language, i'll coordinate with Arielle offline.
[00:09:52] Arielle Chen: thanks Sofia — we'll route legal to legal.
[00:10:00] Liam Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[00:10:03] (meeting continues with some side technical clarifications and brief crosstalk; transcript clipped for brevity)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings ("K V cash" instead of KV cache, small name confusions), speaker overlaps and truncated sentences; audio quality medium.
